title: The Foreskin
notes: This chapter delivers a clean, law-positive decode of the foreskin from Colossians 2:11, testing the blocking-flesh definition across heart, ear, lips, fruit, and Stephen before closing on the Genesis cut-or-be-cut-off wordplay. The member-by-member assembly is dense and on-voice, with a strong return to Jeremiah’s plow-and-knife pair. Residual defects are limited to two author-prose sentence openings banned by house style (That / And) and one director-cue hedge that undercuts the seed-placement observation. No doctrine, scripture-quote, or modernism problems appear. Surgical one-line fixes restore assertiveness without reopening the argument.

proposals.old: That is the foreskin's meaning, stated out loud: the sym:sym-foreskin[foreskin] is the blocking flesh — the layer of the natural man that covers a covenant member and stops its work.
proposals.new: This is the foreskin's meaning, stated out loud: the sym:sym-foreskin[foreskin] is the blocking flesh — the layer of the natural man that covers a covenant member and stops its work.
proposals.summary: Author-prose sentence may not open with That.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids starting author sentences with That. One-word swap to This preserves anaphora and density.

proposals.old: And when God himself performs the surgery, the freed function is love: __“the LORD thy God will circumcise thine heart… *to* sym:sym-love[love] *the LORD thy God with all thine heart*, and with all thy soul, that thou mayest live”__ (Deuteronomy 30:6).
proposals.new: When God himself performs the surgery, the freed function is love: __“the LORD thy God will circumcise thine heart… *to* sym:sym-love[love] *the LORD thy God with all thine heart*, and with all thy soul, that thou mayest live”__ (Deuteronomy 30:6).
proposals.summary: Author-prose sentence may not open with And.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids starting author sentences with And. Dropping the conjunction keeps the claim and the scripture markup intact.

proposals.old: The sign's placement teaches too, though mark this as observation rather than derivation: the literal mark sits on the member where *seed* passes, and the seed, in the language of this book, is the word.
proposals.new: The sign's placement teaches too: the literal mark sits on the member where *seed* passes, and the seed, in the language of this book, is the word.
proposals.rationale: “Mark this as observation rather than derivation” is forbidden presenter staging and hedging. The colon alone asserts the placement lesson without undercutting it.
